<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Property and Equipment</i></b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>, net</i></b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Property and equipment<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">, net are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation and are depreciated over the estimated useful lives of the assets (ranging from <em data-td-fact-id="27405598" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="27405599" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">five</em> years) using the straight-line method. Leasehold improvements are amortized over the estimated useful life of the asset or the lease term, whichever is shorter.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In accordance with <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">the Property, Plant and Equipment Topic of the FASB Accounting Standards Codification (&ldquo;ASC&rdquo;)</font><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">, if indicators of impairment exist, we assess the recoverability of the affected long-lived assets by determining whether the carrying value of such assets can be recovered through undiscounted future operating cash flows. If impairment is indicated, we measure the amount of such impairment by comparing the fair value to the carrying value. There have been <em data-td-fact-id="27405600" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> indicators of impairment through <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017.</em></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Deferred Rent</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Rent expense is recorded on a straight-line basis over the term of <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">any lease. The difference between rent expense accrued and amounts paid under any lease agreement is recorded as deferred rent in the accompanying balance sheets.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Leasehold Incentive Obligation</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In conjunction with <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">the lease agreement covering the facility occupied by us, we received a tenant improvement allowance of <em data-td-fact-id="27405601" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$155</em> per square foot leased, or <em data-td-fact-id="27405602" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$10.1</em> million. As the tenant improvements were constructed, we recorded both the covered tenant improvements (as property and equipment) and an offsetting leasehold incentive obligation on our balance sheet. Through the term of the lease, we record depreciation expense to depreciate the tenant improvements and record an offsetting reduction to rent expense to amortize the leasehold incentive obligation.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>&nbsp;</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Revenue Recognition</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Development Revenues</i></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Development revenues are based on our product discovery, development and commercialization collaboration agreements. Some of our collaboration agreements contain multiple elements, including technological and territorial licenses and research and development services. In accordance with these agreements, we <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>be eligible for license fees, research and development funding, development milestone payments, cost reimbursements, royalty payments, minimum periodic royalty payments and commercial milestone payments. Development revenues include revenues from license fees, research and development funding, the achievement of development milestones and cost reimbursements.</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Pursuant to the Revenue Recognition <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&ndash; Multiple-Element Arrangements Topic of the FASB ASC, each required deliverable is evaluated to determine if it qualifies as a separate unit of accounting. For us, this determination is generally based on whether the deliverable has &ldquo;stand-alone value&rdquo; to the customer. The arrangement&rsquo;s consideration is then allocated to each separate unit of accounting based on the relative selling price of each deliverable. The estimated selling price of each deliverable is determined using the following hierarchy of values: (i)&nbsp;vendor-specific objective evidence of fair value; (ii)&nbsp;<em data-td-fact-id="27405603" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em>-party evidence of selling price; and (iii)&nbsp;best estimate of selling price, or BESP. The BESP reflects our best estimate of what the selling price would be if the deliverable was regularly sold by us on a stand-alone basis. We expect, in general, to use the BESP for allocating consideration to each deliverable. In general, the consideration allocated to each unit of accounting is then recognized as the related goods or services are delivered, limited to the consideration that is <em data-td-fact-id="27405604" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> contingent upon future deliverables. For multiple-element arrangements entered into prior to <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January&nbsp;</em><em data-td-fact-id="27405605" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27405606" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2011</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405607" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> materially modified thereafter, we continue to apply our prior accounting policy with respect to such arrangements. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">59</div>

<hr style="border: currentColor; border-image: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); page-break-after: always; background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
<div id="PGHDR" style="width: 100%; text-align: left;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Non-refundable license fees, if <em data-td-fact-id="27405608" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> associated with our future performance, are recognized when received. Non-refundable license fees, if associated with our future performance obligations, are attributed to a specific program or collaboration and recognized over the period of service for that specific program or collaboration. Amounts received for research funding are recognized as revenues as the services are performed. Revenue is deferred for fees received before earned. Revenues from development milestones are accounted for in accordance with the Revenue Recognition <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&ndash; Milestone Method Topic of the FASB ASC. Milestones are recognized when earned, as evidenced by written acknowledgment from the collaborator or other persuasive evidence that the milestone has been achieved, provided that the milestone event is substantive. A milestone event is considered to be substantive if its achievability was <em data-td-fact-id="27405609" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> reasonably assured at the inception of the agreement and our efforts led to the achievement of the milestone or the milestone was due upon the occurrence of a specific outcome resulting from our performance. If these criteria are <em data-td-fact-id="27405610" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> met, the milestone payment is recognized over the remaining minimum period of our performance obligations under the agreement. We assess whether a milestone is substantive at the inception of each agreement. Revenues from cost reimbursement are recognized when earned, as evidenced by written acknowledgment from the collaborator or other persuasive evidence.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Commercial Revenues</i></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Commercial revenues from collaboration agreements include <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">license payments and royalties on sales made by our collaborators of products incorporating our flavor ingredients, minimum periodic royalty payments and revenues from the achievement of commercial milestones. Commercial revenues also include direct sales of our flavor ingredients to flavor companies. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Royalties on sales made by our collaborators of products incorporating our flavor ingredients are recognized when a royalty report or other persuasive evidence is received, which is generally <em data-td-fact-id="27405611" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> quarter in arrears. Non-refundable minimum periodic royalty payments are recognized as revenues over the related royalty periods. Royalty terms are specific to each collaboration and collaborator and can vary from year to year. These terms vary based on factors such as the characteristics of the flavor ingredient and the product categories and geographies licensed by the collaborator. Periodically, as contractually specified, our collaborators are required to provide a report detailing all sales of products containing our flavor ingredients. To the extent that calculated royalties on sales of such products exceed the minimum periodic royalty payments made to date, the collaborators are required to remit to us the difference between royalties calculated and minimum periodic royalty payments made to date. We recognize this difference as royalties on product sales at the time the report is received. To the extent that minimum periodic royalty payments through the end of any applicable period exceed calculated royalties, we are <em data-td-fact-id="27405612" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> required to refund the difference. Revenues from commercial milestones are recognized when earned, as evidenced by written acknowledgment from the collaborator or other persuasive evidence that the milestone has been achieved, because we have <em data-td-fact-id="27405613" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> further performance obligations related to the commercial milestones.</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Revenues from direct sales of our flavor ingredients are recorded when there is persuasive evidence that an arrangement exists, title has passed, collection is reasonably assured and the price is fixed or determinable. We generally do <em data-td-fact-id="27405614" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> offer discounts, rebates or a general right of return on sales of flavor ingredients.<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>New Accounting Guidance</i></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> May 2014, </em>the FASB issued accounting guidance on the recognition of revenue from customers, which will replace most existing revenue recognition guidance in U.S. GAAP when it becomes effective. Under this guidance, an entity will recognize revenue when it transfers promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects that the entity expects in exchange for the goods or services. This guidance also requires more detailed disclosures to enable users of the financial statements to understand the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows arising from contracts with customers. The guidance is currently effective for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2017, </em>and interim periods within those years. The guidance allows entities to select <em data-td-fact-id="27405615" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> of <em data-td-fact-id="27405616" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em> methods of adoption, either the full retrospective approach, meaning the guidance would be applied to all periods presented, or modified retrospective, meaning the cumulative effect of applying the guidance would be recognized as an adjustment to our opening retained earnings new balance at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018, </em>along with providing certain additional disclosures. We will adopt the new standard on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018 </em>and elect the modified retrospective method of adoption. Our current analysis indicates that the new standard <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">will impact the timing of recognition for royalty revenues associated with sales made by collaborators, requiring recognition earlier than historically recorded. We anticipate that the cumulative effect of the new guidance will be an adjustment to our opening retained earnings on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2018 </em>of approximately <em data-td-fact-id="27405617" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.5</em> million to reflect royalty revenues that would have been recorded in the <em data-td-fact-id="27405618" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="27405619" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2018</em> under previous revenue recognition guidance.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">60</div>

</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Direct Sales</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Our direct sales <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">revenues were <em data-td-fact-id="27405620" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.8</em> million, <em data-td-fact-id="27405621" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.1</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="27405622" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$640,000</em> for the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27405623" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405624" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Cost of Commercial Revenues</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Cost of c<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">ommercial revenues represents royalties payable under our <em data-td-fact-id="27405625" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em>-party licensing agreements and the cost of goods sold related to direct sales, including related shipping and handling costs. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Research</i></b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>, </i></b><b><i>D</i></b><b><i>evelopment</i></b><b><i> and Patents</i></b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Research<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> and development costs, including those incurred in relation to our collaborative agreements, are expensed in the period incurred. Research and development costs primarily consist of salaries and related expenses for personnel, facilities and depreciation, research and development supplies, licenses and outside services. Such research and development costs totaled <em data-td-fact-id="27405626" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$15.0</em> million, <em data-td-fact-id="27405627" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$19.3</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="27405628" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$22.4</em> million for the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27405629" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405630" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Costs related to filing and pursuing patent applications are expensed as incurred, as recoverability of such expenditures is uncertain<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">. We include all external costs related to the filing of patents related to development in Research, Development and Patents expenses. Such patent-related expenses totaled <em data-td-fact-id="27405631" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.7</em> million for each of the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27405632" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405633" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015.</em> Costs to maintain existing patents are expensed to selling, general and administrative expense as incurred. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Employee Benefit Plans</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">We<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> have a defined contribution plan under Section <em data-td-fact-id="27405634" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">401</em>(k) of the Internal Revenue Code covering employees who meet certain eligibility requirements. Eligible employees <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>defer their pre-tax compensation up to the maximum allowed by the Internal Revenue Service, or IRS. Under the plan, we <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>match a portion of employee contributions up to a defined maximum. Such matching contributions become vested and non-forfeitable according to a defined vesting schedule. We made matching contributions of <em data-td-fact-id="27405635" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$124,000,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27405636" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$166,000</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405637" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$183,000</em> for the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27405638" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405639" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">61</div>

<hr style="border: currentColor; border-image: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); page-break-after: always; background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
<div id="PGHDR" style="width: 100%; text-align: left;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Expected volatility is based on <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">our historical volatility. The risk-free interest rate for the expected term of the option is based on the average United States&nbsp;Treasury yield curve at the grant date. The assumed dividend yield is based on our expectation of <em data-td-fact-id="27405640" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> paying dividends in the foreseeable future. The expected term of options granted is based on historical exercise data<i>. </i></font><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The assumptions related to expected volatility and risk-free interest rate used for the valuation of stock options differ from those used for the valuation of employee stock purchase plan rights primarily due to the difference in their respective expected terms.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>&nbsp;</i></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The weighted-average estimated fair value of stock options granted during the years ended <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27405641" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405642" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> were <em data-td-fact-id="27405643" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.68,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27405644" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.70</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405645" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2.79</em> per share, respectively. The weighted-average estimated fair value of employee stock purchase plan rights granted during the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27405646" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405647" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> were <em data-td-fact-id="27405648" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.38,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27405649" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.74</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405650" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2.88</em> per share, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> March 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="27405651" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27405652" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09,</em> <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting</i>. This guidance simplifies how several aspects of share-based payments are accounted for and presented in the financial statements. This guidance is effective beginning <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> January 1, 2017 </em>and we adopted this ASU in the <em data-td-fact-id="27405653" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="27405654" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017.</em> We have excess tax benefits for which a benefit could <em data-td-fact-id="27405655" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be previously recognized of approximately <em data-td-fact-id="27405656" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$3.2</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="27405657" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$243,000</em> for Federal and California purposes, respectively. The balance of the unrecognized excess tax benefits are reversed with the impact recorded to retained earnings, including a change to the valuation allowance. Due to the full valuation allowance on our deferred tax assets, there was <em data-td-fact-id="27405658" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> impact to the financial statements as a result of this adoption. Additionally, ASU <em data-td-fact-id="27405659" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27405660" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">09</em> amends existing guidance to allow forfeitures of share-based awards to be recognized as they occur. Previous guidance required that share-based compensation expense include an estimate of forfeitures. We made a policy election to account for forfeitures as they occur. The cumulative effect of adoption was an increase of <em data-td-fact-id="27405661" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$88,000</em> to both additional paid-in capital and accumulated deficit. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">S<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">tock-based compensation expenses for options and awards are recognized on a straight-line basis. S</font><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">tock-based compensation expenses are allocated to research, development and patents or selling, general and administrative based upon the department to which the associated employee or non-employee reports. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Total stock-based compensation expense<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">s recognized for the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27405662" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405663" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> was comprised as follows (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The total fair value of options that vested during the years ended <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27405664" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405665" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> was <em data-td-fact-id="27405666" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$3.4</em> million, <em data-td-fact-id="27405667" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$4.0</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="27405668" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5.8</em> million, respectively. At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em>total unrecognized estimated compensation expenses related to non-vested stock options granted prior to that date were <em data-td-fact-id="27405669" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$2.2</em> million, expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of <em data-td-fact-id="27405670" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1.8</em> years.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Income Taxes</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">W<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">e account for income taxes in accordance with provisions which set forth an asset and liability approach that requires the recognition of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities for the expected future tax consequences of temporary differences between the carrying amounts and the tax bases of assets and liabilities. Valuation allowances are established when necessary to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount that is more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="27405671" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> expected to be realized. In making such a determination, a review of all available positive and negative evidence is considered, including scheduled reversal of deferred tax liabilities, projected future taxable income, tax planning strategies and recent financial performance. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">62</div>

<hr style="border: currentColor; border-image: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); page-break-after: always; background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
<div id="PGHDR" style="width: 100%; text-align: left;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">T<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">he provisions of the Income Taxes Topic of the FASB ASC defines a recognition threshold and measurement attributes for financial statement recognition and measurement of a tax provision taken or expected to be taken in a tax return. The Topic also provides guidance on de-recognition, classification, interest and penalties, accounting in interim periods, disclosure and transition. Under the Topic, the impact of an uncertain income tax position on the income tax return must be recognized at the largest amount that is more-likely-than-<em data-td-fact-id="27405672" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> to be sustained upon audit by the relevant taxing authority. An uncertain income tax position will <em data-td-fact-id="27405673" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> be recognized if it has less than a <em data-td-fact-id="27405674" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">50%</em> likelihood of being sustained. We recognize interest and penalties related to uncertain tax positions as a component of the income tax provision.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Net Loss Per Share</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Basic earnings per share (&ldquo;EPS&rdquo;) is calculated by dividing the net loss by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding for the period, without consideration for common stock equivalents. Diluted EPS is computed by dividing the net income or loss by the weighted average number of common share equivalents outstanding for the period determined using the treasury-stock method<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">. Dilutive common share equivalents include the dilutive effect of in-the-money shares, which is calculated based on the average share price for each period using the treasury stock method. Under the treasury stock method, the exercise price of a share, the amount of compensation cost, if any, for future service that we have <em data-td-fact-id="27405675" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> yet recognized, and the amount of estimated tax benefits that would be recorded in paid-in capital, if any, when the share is exercised are assumed to be used to repurchase shares in the current period. For purposes of this calculation, options to purchase common stock are considered to be common stock equivalents and are only included in the calculation of diluted EPS when their effect is dilutive.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The following table sets forth the computatio<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">n of basic and diluted net loss per share for the respective periods. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Comprehensive Income (Loss)</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>&nbsp;</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Comprehensive Income Topic of the FASB ASC<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> requires that all components of comprehensive income (loss), including net income (loss), be reported in the financial statements in the period in which they are recognized. Comprehensive income (loss) is defined as the change in equity during a period from transactions and other events and circumstances from non-owner sources. Our accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27405676" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405677" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015</em> consisted of unrealized gains or losses on investments available-for-sale and is reported in stockholders&rsquo; equity.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Segment Reporting</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">We<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> operate in <em data-td-fact-id="27405678" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> business segment, which is the development and commercialization of flavor ingredients. All of our operations are located in the United States. Due to the confidential nature of our collaborations, it is impracticable to report geographic information related to revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</i></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> February 2016, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em data-td-fact-id="27405679" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27405680" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02,</em> <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Leases (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="27405681" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">842</em>) </i>in order to increase transparency and comparability among organizations by recognizing lease assets and lease liabilities on the balance sheet for those leases classified as operating leases under previous GAAP. ASU <em data-td-fact-id="27405682" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27405683" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02</em> requires that a lessee should recognize a liability to make lease payments (the lease liability) and a right-of-use asset representing its right to use the underlying asset for the lease term on the balance sheet. ASU <em data-td-fact-id="27405684" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27405685" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02</em> is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 15, 2018 (</em>including interim periods within those periods) using a modified retrospective approach and early adoption is permitted. The Company will adopt ASU <em data-td-fact-id="27405686" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27405687" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">02</em> in the <em data-td-fact-id="27405688" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="27405689" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2019.</em> Although the Company is in the process of evaluating the impact of adoption of the ASU on its consolidated financial statements, the Company currently believes the most significant changes will be related to the recognition of new right-of-use assets and lease liabilities on the Company&#39;s balance sheet for real estate operating leases.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
</div>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="6604" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519218778059" id="thunderdome-statement-797251">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27405690" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2.</em> Balance Sheet Details</b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Short-term </i></b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Investments Available-for-Sale</i></b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The following is a summary of <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">short-term investments available-for-sale securities at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 (</em>in&nbsp;thousands): </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-taggable-table="table" data-td-v2v-id="1519218778055" id="thunderdome-statement-797252">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="finTable" id="null" style="width: 95%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: Times New Roman,Times,serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-right: 5%; margin-left: 45pt;">

		<tr style="vertical-align: bottom;">

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">We believe that the decline in value of these securities is temporary and primarily related to the change in market interest rates since purchase and that it is more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="27405691" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> that we will be able to hold these securities to maturity. Therefore we anticipate full recovery of their amortized cost basis at maturity.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="6605" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519218785643" id="thunderdome-statement-797257">
<p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt; text-align: left; text-indent: -36pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27405699" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em></b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>.</b><b> </b><b>Fair Value Disclosures</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The following table<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> presents information about our financial assets and financial liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and indicates the fair value hierarchy of the valuation techniques we use to determine such fair value. In general, fair values determined by Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405700" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em> inputs use quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that we have the ability to access. We classify money market funds and United States Treasuries as Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405701" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em> assets. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Fair values determined by Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405702" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> inputs utilize inputs other than quoted prices included in Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405703" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em> that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405704" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> inputs include quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, and inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability, such as interest rates and yield curves that are observable at commonly quoted intervals. We obtain the fair value of Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405705" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> financial instruments from a <em data-td-fact-id="27405706" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em>-party professional pricing service using quoted market prices for identical or comparable instruments. The professional pricing service gathers market prices from a variety of industry standard data providers, security master files from large financial institutions and other <em data-td-fact-id="27405707" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">third</em>-party sources. The service uses these multiple prices as inputs into a distribution-curve based algorithm to determine a fair value. We then validate the quoted fair values provided by the professional pricing service by comparing the service&rsquo;s assessment of the fair values of our Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405708" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> investment portfolio balance against the fair values of our Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405709" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> investment portfolio balance provided by our investment managers. We classify United States government agency securities and corporate debt securities as Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405710" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> assets. There were <em data-td-fact-id="27405711" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">no</em> transfers between Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405712" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">1</em> and Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405713" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2</em> during <em data-td-fact-id="27405714" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2017</em> or <em data-td-fact-id="27405715" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016.</em></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">65</div>

<hr style="border: currentColor; border-image: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); page-break-after: always; background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
<div id="PGHDR" style="width: 100%; text-align: left;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405716" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em> inputs are unobservable inputs for the <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">asset or liability, and include situations where there is little, if any, market activity for the asset or liability. In certain cases, the inputs used to measure fair value <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>fall into different&nbsp;levels of the fair value hierarchy.&nbsp;In such&nbsp;cases, the level in the fair value hierarchy within which the fair value measurement in its entirety falls has been determined based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement&nbsp;in its entirety.&nbsp;Our assessment of the significance of a particular input to the fair value measurement in its entirety requires judgment, and we consider factors specific&nbsp;to the asset or liability. We do <em data-td-fact-id="27405717" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> hold any Level <em data-td-fact-id="27405718" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">3</em> assets or liabilities.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The fair value as of <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27405719" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> for assets that have recurring measurements are shown below (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="6606" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519218793794" id="thunderdome-statement-797260">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27405720" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4.</em> Product Discovery</b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>,</b><b> Development </b><b>and Commercialization </b><b>Collaborations</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Our<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> current collaboration agreements generally provide for research and development funding, milestone payments, cost reimbursement and royalty payments in the event the collaborator commercializes a product incorporating our flavor ingredients.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Development milestones are generally due upon selection and regulatory events. Development milestones are considered to be due to our performance and are accounted for as substantive milestones in accordance with the Revenue Recognition &ndash; Milestone Method Topic of the FASB ASC. Development milestones are recorded as development revenues. An example of a selection event would be a collaborator selecting a compound for development. An example of a regulatory event would be a selected compound obtaining either U.S. or foreign regulatory approval. There are circumstances under which we and our collaborators in the future <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>mutually agree to pursue additional program goals, in which case we could then be eligible to earn additional development milestones. Any such additional milestones remain uncertain at this time. </font><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Development milestones generally range in value up to <em data-td-fact-id="27405721" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$750,000</em> each. We</font><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> do <em data-td-fact-id="27405722" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> consider any individual development milestone to be material due to the relatively small size of any individual development milestone payment in relation to our annual revenues, and due to the uncertainty associated with the scientific progress required for us to earn such milestones.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">66</div>

<hr style="border: currentColor; border-image: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); page-break-after: always; background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
<div id="PGHDR" style="width: 100%; text-align: left;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Commercial milestones are generally due upon commercial events. <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">We do <em data-td-fact-id="27405723" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> consider commercial events to be due to our performance, and as such, are <em data-td-fact-id="27405724" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">not</em> accounted for as substantive milestones in accordance with the Revenue Recognition &ndash; Milestone Method Topic of the FASB ASC. Examples of commercial events would be the <em data-td-fact-id="27405725" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">first</em> commercial sale of a product containing a developed compound or upon sales of a product containing a developed compound reaching a certain level. There are circumstances under which we and our collaborators in the future <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> may </em>mutually agree to pursue additional program goals, in which case we could then be eligible to earn additional commercial milestones. Any such additional milestones remain uncertain at this time. </font><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Commercial milestones generally range in value up to <em data-td-fact-id="27405726" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1.5</em> million each. We</font><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> consider milestones for commercial events to be commercial revenues. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The specific type of royalty and method for calculating royalty payments varies by agreement<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">. We have retail-based royalty agreements, where any potential royalty payable to us is calculated as a percentage of the net sales price of a manufacturer&rsquo;s finished products or is based on the volume of a manufacturer&rsquo;s finished product that it sells. Our retail-based royalty agreements provide for an effective royalty rate of up to <em data-td-fact-id="27405727" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">4%.</em> Our agreements with Ajinomoto and PepsiCo are either exclusively or partially retail-based royalty agreements. We have ingredient supply agreements, where any potential royalty payable to us is calculated as a percentage of the sales price of either our ingredient itself or the flavor system in which our ingredient is contained or is based on the volume of the ingredient itself used by a manufacturer in a finished product. Our ingredient supply royalty agreements specify royalty rates that are typically greater than the rates specified by our retail-based agreements. Our agreements with Firmenich and PepsiCo are either exclusively or partially ingredient supply-based royalty agreements. Certain of our current collaboration agreements also provide for upfront license fees and minimum periodic royalties. Below is a discussion of our material agreements. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Material Agreements</i></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Firmenich</i><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i> (Sweet)</i><i>. </i>In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July 2009, </em>we entered into a collaboration agreement with Firmenich to work for a minimum <em data-td-fact-id="27405728" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">two</em>-year collaborative period to discover novel flavor ingredients intended to modify the sweet taste of sucrose, fructose or various forms of rebaudioside. The agreement includes <em data-td-fact-id="27405729" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> consecutive options of <em data-td-fact-id="27405730" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">one</em> year each that could further extend the collaborative research funding period. The agreement was subsequently amended in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> October 2009. </em>Under the agreement as amended, Firmenich agreed to pay a license fee, payable in <em data-td-fact-id="27405731" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em> installments, research and development fees and specified payments upon the achievement of milestones. In the event of commercialization, we are entitled to receive royalties on future sales of products containing a discovered flavor ingredient. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> October 2010</em><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">, we and Firmenich further amended the agreement to include, among other things, commercial development of <em data-td-fact-id="27405732" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">S6973,</em> our novel sucrose modifier, for specific beverage applications. The amendment also converts Firmenich&rsquo;s license for use of <em data-td-fact-id="27405733" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">S6973</em> in powdered beverages from co-exclusive to exclusive and grants Firmenich an exclusive right to commercialize any compound that they select for development for use in confectionary food products. In return, under the terms of the amendment we received an additional license fee, and incremental milestone payments and minimum annual royalties.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> November 2010, </em>Firmenich <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">exercised its option to expand the companies&rsquo; agreement to include the discovery, development, and worldwide commercialization of natural flavor ingredients that modify the taste of sucrose, fructose, and various forms of rebaudioside. In consideration of the expansion of the agreement, Firmenich paid us additional research funding as well as milestones, minimum annual royalties, and royalties on sales of natural sweet enhancers developed under the collaboration.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> April 2013, </em><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">we amended and restated the collaboration agreement with Firmenich </font><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">to extend the collaborative research period through <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July 2016, </em>subject to limited termination rights. Firmenich paid an additional non-refundable license fee of <em data-td-fact-id="27405734" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$5</em> million, of which <em data-td-fact-id="27405735" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$4</em> million was paid in <em data-td-fact-id="27405736" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2013</em> and the remaining <em data-td-fact-id="27405737" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$1</em> million was paid at the end of the research period. Firmenich also paid approximately <em data-td-fact-id="27405738" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$13</em>&nbsp;million in research funding over the <em data-td-fact-id="27405739" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">three</em>-year extension period from <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July 2013 </em>through <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> July 2016. </em></font><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Firmenich continues to have obligations for other milestone payments, cost reimbursements and royalty payments under an increased royalty rate structure based upon Firmenich sales of flavor ingredients developed under the collaboration. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In connection with this collaborative agreement, <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">we recognized development revenues of <em data-td-fact-id="27405740" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$0.3</em> million, <em data-td-fact-id="27405741" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$3.7</em> million and <em data-td-fact-id="27405742" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">$6.2</em> million for the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27405743" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27405744" style="font-weight: inherit; font-style: normal;">2015,</em> respectively. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">67</div>
